## Problem 1

### (a)
```{r}
#' Validate a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object.
#' @return TRUE if valid, otherwise a character vector of errors.
validate_waldCI <- function(object) {
  errors <- character()

  if (length(object@estimate) != 1L ||
      any(!is.finite(object@estimate))) {
    errors <- c(errors, "Mean must be a single finite number.")
  }

  if (length(object@se) != 1L ||
      any(!is.finite(object@se)) ||
      any(object@se < 0)) {
    errors <- c(
      errors,
      "Standard error must be a single finite nonnegative number."
    )
  }

  if (length(object@conf_level) != 1L ||
      any(!is.finite(object@conf_level)) ||
      any(object@conf_level <= 0 | object@conf_level >= 1)) {
    errors <- c(
      errors,
      "Confidence level must be a single number strictly between 0 and 1."
    )
  }

  if (length(errors) > 0L) {
    return(errors)
  }

  margin <- qnorm(
    (1 - object@conf_level) / 2,
    lower.tail = FALSE
  ) * object@se

  bounds <- object@estimate + c(-margin, margin)

  if (any(!is.finite(bounds))) {
    return("Confidence interval bounds must be finite.")
  }

  TRUE
}

setClass(
  "waldCI",
  slots = c(
    estimate = "numeric",
    se = "numeric",
    conf_level = "numeric"
  ),
  validity = validate_waldCI
)

isClass("waldCI")
```

```{r}
#' Construct a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param level Confidence level strictly between 0 and 1.
#' @param mean Estimated mean; supply together with sterr.
#' @param sterr Nonnegative standard error.
#' @param lb Lower bound; supply together with ub.
#' @param ub Upper bound.
#' @return A valid waldCI object.
make_waldCI <- function(level, mean = NULL, sterr = NULL,
                        lb = NULL, ub = NULL) {
  if (!is.numeric(level) || length(level) != 1L ||
      !is.finite(level) || level <= 0 || level >= 1) {
    stop("level must be a finite number strictly between 0 and 1.")
  }

  use_mean <- !is.null(mean) && !is.null(sterr) &&
    is.null(lb) && is.null(ub)

  use_bounds <- !is.null(lb) && !is.null(ub) &&
    is.null(mean) && is.null(sterr)

  if (!use_mean && !use_bounds) {
    stop("Supply either mean and sterr, or lb and ub, exclusively.")
  }

  inputs <- if (use_mean) list(mean, sterr) else list(lb, ub)

  valid_inputs <- vapply(
    inputs,
    function(x) {
      is.numeric(x) && length(x) == 1L && is.finite(x)
    },
    logical(1)
  )

  if (!all(valid_inputs)) {
    stop("Inputs must be single finite numbers.")
  }

  if (use_bounds) {
    if (lb > ub) {
      stop("lb must not exceed ub.")
    }

    z <- qnorm((1 - level) / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
    mean <- lb / 2 + ub / 2
    sterr <- (ub / 2 - lb / 2) / z
  }

  object <- new(
    "waldCI",
    estimate = as.numeric(mean),
    se = as.numeric(sterr),
    conf_level = as.numeric(level)
  )

  validObject(object)
  object
}

validObject(make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 17.2, ub = 24.7))
validObject(make_waldCI(level = 0.99, mean = 13, sterr = 2.5))
```
```{r}
#' Access components of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object.
#' @return A numeric scalar containing the requested component.
setGeneric("lb", function(object) standardGeneric("lb"))
setGeneric("ub", function(object) standardGeneric("ub"))
setGeneric("sterr", function(object) standardGeneric("sterr"))
setGeneric("level", function(object) standardGeneric("level"))

setMethod("lb", "waldCI", function(object) {
  z <- qnorm((1 - object@conf_level) / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
  object@estimate - z * object@se
})

setMethod("ub", "waldCI", function(object) {
  z <- qnorm((1 - object@conf_level) / 2, lower.tail = FALSE)
  object@estimate + z * object@se
})

setMethod("sterr", "waldCI", function(object) {
  object@se
})

setMethod("level", "waldCI", function(object) {
  object@conf_level
})

#' Extract the mean of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param x A waldCI object.
#' @param ... Additional arguments, unused.
#' @return The estimated mean.
setMethod("mean", "waldCI", function(x, ...) {
  x@estimate
})

#' Display a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object.
#' @return NULL invisibly; prints the interval and its components.
setMethod("show", "waldCI", function(object) {
  cat(sprintf(
    "%.1f%% Wald confidence interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
    100 * level(object), lb(object), ub(object)
  ))
  cat(sprintf(
    "Mean: %.4f; Standard error: %.4f\n",
    mean(object), sterr(object)
  ))
  invisible(NULL)
})

make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 17.2, ub = 24.7)
```

```{r}
#' Modify components of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object.
#' @param value A single finite numeric replacement value.
#' @return A validated waldCI object.
#' @details Bound setters preserve the opposite bound and confidence level.
#' Other setters preserve the remaining stored parameters.
setGeneric("lb<-", function(object, value) standardGeneric("lb<-"))
setGeneric("ub<-", function(object, value) standardGeneric("ub<-"))
setGeneric("mean<-", function(object, value) standardGeneric("mean<-"))
setGeneric("sterr<-", function(object, value) standardGeneric("sterr<-"))
setGeneric("level<-", function(object, value) standardGeneric("level<-"))

setReplaceMethod("lb", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  make_waldCI(level = level(object), lb = value, ub = ub(object))
})

setReplaceMethod("ub", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  make_waldCI(level = level(object), lb = lb(object), ub = value)
})

setReplaceMethod("mean", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  make_waldCI(
    level = level(object),
    mean = value,
    sterr = sterr(object)
  )
})

setReplaceMethod("sterr", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  make_waldCI(
    level = level(object),
    mean = mean(object),
    sterr = value
  )
})

setReplaceMethod("level", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  make_waldCI(
    level = value,
    mean = mean(object),
    sterr = sterr(object)
  )
})

test_ci <- make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 17.2, ub = 24.7)
lb(test_ci) <- 18
test_ci
validObject(test_ci)
```

```{r}
#' Check whether values lie within a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object.
#' @param value A numeric vector of values to check.
#' @return A logical vector; missing values produce NA.
setGeneric(
  "contains",
  function(object, value) standardGeneric("contains")
)

setMethod("contains", "waldCI", function(object, value) {
  if (!is.numeric(value)) {
    stop("value must be numeric.")
  }
  value >= lb(object) & value <= ub(object)
})

#' Check whether two Wald confidence intervals overlap
#'
#' @param x,y waldCI objects.
#' @return A single logical value; touching endpoints count as overlap.
setGeneric("overlap", function(x, y) standardGeneric("overlap"))

setMethod(
  "overlap",
  signature(x = "waldCI", y = "waldCI"),
  function(x, y) {
    lb(x) <= ub(y) && lb(y) <= ub(x)
  }
)

#' Extract the bounds of a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param x A waldCI object.
#' @return A numeric vector containing the lower and upper bounds.
setGeneric("as.numeric")

setMethod("as.numeric", "waldCI", function(x) {
  c(lb(x), ub(x))
})

contains(test_ci, c(17, 18, 20, 24.7, 25))
overlap(test_ci, make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 24, ub = 30))
as.numeric(test_ci)
```

```{r}
#' Transform a Wald confidence interval
#'
#' @param object A waldCI object.
#' @param fun A scalar numeric function monotonic over the interval.
#' @return A waldCI object with transformed bounds and unchanged level.
#' @details Monotonicity is the caller's responsibility. The new mean
#' is the midpoint of the transformed bounds, and its standard error
#' is reconstructed from those bounds.
setGeneric(
  "transformCI",
  function(object, fun) standardGeneric("transformCI")
)

setMethod("transformCI", "waldCI", function(object, fun) {
  if (!is.function(fun)) {
    stop("fun must be a function.")
  }

  warning(
    "Only functions monotonic over the entire interval make sense; ",
    "monotonicity is not checked.",
    call. = FALSE
  )

  bounds <- vapply(
    as.numeric(object),
    function(x) {
      result <- fun(x)
      if (!is.numeric(result) || length(result) != 1L ||
          !is.finite(result)) {
        stop("fun must return a single finite number at each endpoint.")
      }
      result
    },
    numeric(1)
  )

  make_waldCI(
    level = level(object),
    lb = min(bounds),
    ub = max(bounds)
  )
})

transformCI(
  make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 4, ub = 9),
  sqrt
)
```

### (b)

```{r}
ci1 <- make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 17.2, ub = 24.7)
ci2 <- make_waldCI(level = 0.99, mean = 13, sterr = 2.5)
ci3 <- make_waldCI(level = 0.75, lb = 27.43, ub = 39.22)

ci1
ci2
ci3

as.numeric(ci1)
as.numeric(ci2)
as.numeric(ci3)

lb(ci2)
ub(ci2)
mean(ci1)
sterr(ci3)
level(ci2)

lb(ci2) <- 10.5
mean(ci3) <- 34
level(ci3) <- 0.8

contains(ci1, 17)
contains(ci3, 44)
overlap(ci1, ci2)

eci1 <- transformCI(ci1, sqrt)
eci1
mean(transformCI(ci2, log))
```
The containment checks both returned FALSE, while ci1 and the updated ci2 overlapped. The square-root transformation of ci1 produced [4.1473, 4.9699]. Transformed objects use the midpoint of the transformed bounds as their mean.

### (c)

```{r}
#' Report whether an invalid operation is rejected
#'
#' @param expr An expression expected to produce an error.
#' @return A message indicating rejection or unexpected acceptance.
check_invalid <- function(expr) {
  tryCatch(
    {
      force(expr)
      "ERROR: Invalid input was accepted."
    },
    error = function(e) {
      paste("Rejected:", conditionMessage(e))
    }
  )
}

invalid_checks <- c(
  negative_se = check_invalid(
    make_waldCI(level = 0.95, mean = 10, sterr = -1)
  ),
  reversed_bounds = check_invalid(
    make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 20, ub = 10)
  ),
  infinite_bounds = check_invalid(
    make_waldCI(level = 0.95, lb = 0, ub = Inf)
  ),
  invalid_lb_setter = check_invalid({
    x <- ci1
    lb(x) <- 30
  }),
  invalid_ub_setter = check_invalid({
    x <- ci1
    ub(x) <- 10
  }),
  invalid_mean_setter = check_invalid({
    x <- ci1
    mean(x) <- Inf
  }),
  invalid_se_setter = check_invalid({
    x <- ci1
    sterr(x) <- -1
  }),
  invalid_level_setter = check_invalid({
    x <- ci1
    level(x) <- 1
  })
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Test = names(invalid_checks),
    Result = unname(invalid_checks)
  ),
  col.names = c("Invalid operation", "Validation result"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
All eight invalid operations were rejected, including negative standard errors, reversed or infinite bounds, and invalid setter values.

### (a)

### (b)

```{r}
final_winners <- unique(
  tennis[
    round == "F",
    .(tourney_id, winner_id, winner_name)
  ]
)

title_counts <- final_winners[
  , .(titles = .N),
  by = .(winner_id, winner_name)
]

multiple_titles <- title_counts[
  titles > 1
][order(-titles, winner_name)]

knitr::kable(
  multiple_titles[, .(winner_name, titles)],
  col.names = c("Player", "Tournament titles"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

title_summary <- title_counts[
  , .(
    multiple_winners = sum(titles > 1),
    most_titles = max(titles)
  )
]

knitr::kable(
  title_summary,
  col.names = c("Players with multiple titles", "Most titles")
)
```
Twelve players won multiple titles. Dominic Thiem and Novak Djokovic tied for the most, with five each.

### (c)

```{r}
ace_summary <- tennis[
  !is.na(w_ace) & !is.na(l_ace),
  .(
    matches = .N,
    winner_mean = mean(w_ace),
    loser_mean = mean(l_ace),
    mean_difference = mean(w_ace - l_ace),
    winner_more_pct = 100 * mean(w_ace > l_ace),
    tied_pct = 100 * mean(w_ace == l_ace)
  )
]

knitr::kable(
  ace_summary,
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Matches",
    "Winner mean",
    "Loser mean",
    "Mean difference",
    "Winner more (%)",
    "Tied (%)"
  )
)
```
Across 2,694 matches with complete ace data, winners averaged 1.70 more aces than losers and hit more aces in 57.28% of matches. This supports an association between aces and winning, but not causation.

### (d)

```{r}
player_matches <- rbindlist(list(
  tennis[, .(
    player_id = winner_id,
    player = winner_name,
    won = 1L
  )],
  tennis[, .(
    player_id = loser_id,
    player = loser_name,
    won = 0L
  )]
))

player_rates <- player_matches[
  , .(matches = .N, wins = sum(won)),
  by = .(player_id, player)
][matches >= 5]

player_rates[, win_rate := wins / matches]

best_players <- player_rates[
  win_rate == max(win_rate),
  .(player, matches, wins, win_rate_pct = 100 * win_rate)
]

knitr::kable(
  best_players,
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Player", "Matches", "Wins", "Win rate (%)"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
Among players with at least five matches, Rafael Nadal had the highest win rate, winning 60 of 69 matches (86.96%).

## Problem 3

### (a)

```{r}
library(plotly)

if (!file.exists("us-states.csv")) {
  download.file(
    paste0(
      "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nytimes/",
      "covid-19-data/master/rolling-averages/us-states.csv"
    ),
    destfile = "us-states.csv",
    mode = "wb"
  )
}

covid <- fread("us-states.csv")
covid[, date := as.Date(date)]

covid_states <- covid[state %in% state.name]

knitr::kable(
  covid_states[
    , .(
      first_date = min(date),
      last_date = max(date),
      states = uniqueN(state)
    )
  ],
  col.names = c("First date", "Last date", "States")
)
```

```{r}
national_cases <- covid_states[
  , .(daily_cases_avg = sum(cases_avg)),
  by = date
][order(date)]

plot_ly(
  data = national_cases,
  x = ~date,
  y = ~daily_cases_avg,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",
  height = 550,
  line = list(color = "#2166AC", width = 2),
  hovertemplate = paste0(
    "Date: %{x|%Y-%m-%d}",
    "<br>Daily cases: %{y:,.0f}",
    "<extra></extra>"
  )
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "COVID-19 waves in the 50 U.S. states",
      font = list(size = 16)
    ),
    font = list(size = 12),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "",
      tickformat = "%Y-%m",
      dtick = "M6",
      tickangle = 0,
      automargin = TRUE,
      showgrid = FALSE
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = list(text = "Daily cases (7-day average)"),
      tickformat = "~s",
      nticks = 6,
      rangemode = "tozero",
      automargin = TRUE
    ),
    margin = list(l = 75, r = 20, t = 60, b = 60),
    hovermode = "x",
    showlegend = FALSE
  ) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

Source: The New York Times, January 2020–March 2023. Values sum the reported 7-day averages across the 50 states.

I identify approximately eight broad waves, treating nearby fluctuations within a sustained surge as one wave. Using 150,000 daily reported cases as a descriptive peak threshold, three waves were major (winter 2020–21, late summer 2021, and winter 2021–22), while five were smaller. The largest peak occurred in January 2022, at roughly 800,000 cases per day.

### (b)

```{r}
common_dates <- covid_states[
  , .(
    states = uniqueN(state),
    complete = all(is.finite(cases_avg_per_100k))
  ),
  by = date
][states == 50 & complete, date]

rate_data <- covid_states[date %in% common_dates]

state_rates <- rate_data[
  , .(mean_daily_rate = mean(cases_avg_per_100k)),
  by = state
][order(-mean_daily_rate)]

extreme_rates <- rbind(
  state_rates[1, .(state, mean_daily_rate, category = "Highest")],
  state_rates[.N, .(state, mean_daily_rate, category = "Lowest")]
)

knitr::kable(
  data.table(
    first_date = min(common_dates),
    last_date = max(common_dates)
  ),
  col.names = c("Comparison start", "Comparison end")
)

knitr::kable(
  extreme_rates[, .(category, state, mean_daily_rate)],
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "Category", "State",
    "Mean daily cases per 100,000"
  ),
  row.names = FALSE
)

comparison <- rate_data[
  state %in% extreme_rates$state
][order(state, date)]

plot_ly(
  comparison,
  x = ~date,
  y = ~cases_avg_per_100k,
  color = ~state,
  colors = c("#2166AC", "#B2182B"),
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",
  height = 550,
  text = ~state,
  hovertemplate = paste0(
    "%{text}<br>%{x|%Y-%m-%d}",
    "<br>Cases per 100,000: %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>"
  )
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "States with highest and lowest average case rates",
      font = list(size = 15)
    ),
    xaxis = list(
      title = "",
      tickformat = "%Y-%m",
      dtick = "M6",
      tickangle = 0,
      automargin = TRUE
    ),
    yaxis = list(
      title = "Daily cases per 100,000 (7-day average)",
      rangemode = "tozero",
      automargin = TRUE
    ),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.18),

    font = list(size = 12)
  ) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

Source: The New York Times. States are ranked by their mean daily reported case rate over dates with complete observations for all 50 states.

Over the shared observation period, Rhode Island had the highest mean daily reported case rate (39.29 per 100,000), while Maine had the lowest (19.98). Rhode Island had much larger peaks in winter 2020–21 and January 2022, although the states’ rates were closer later. Differences in testing and reporting may also affect this comparison.

### (c)

```{r}
first_crossings <- covid_states[
  is.finite(cases_avg_per_100k) & cases_avg_per_100k >= 1
][order(date),
  .(
    first_date = date[1],
    crossing_rate = cases_avg_per_100k[1]
  ),
  by = state
][order(first_date, -crossing_rate, state)]

earliest_five <- first_crossings[1:5]

knitr::kable(
  earliest_five,
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c(
    "State", "First date reaching threshold",
    "Cases per 100,000 on that date"
  ),

)

early_cases <- covid_states[
  state %in% earliest_five$state &
    date >= as.Date("2020-02-15") &
    date <= as.Date("2020-04-15")
][order(state, date)]

early_cases[
  , plot_rate := fifelse(
    cases_avg_per_100k > 0,
    cases_avg_per_100k,
    NA_real_
  )
]

plot_ly(
  early_cases,
  x = ~date,
  y = ~plot_rate,
  color = ~state,
  colors = c("#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#E69F00"),
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "lines",

  hovertemplate = paste0(
    "%{text}<br>%{x|%Y-%m-%d}",

  )
) |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = "Five states reaching the early-impact threshold first",

    ),
    xaxis = list(

      automargin = TRUE
    ),
    yaxis = list(

      tickvals = c(0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100),
      ticktext = c("0.01", "0.1", "1", "10", "100"),
      automargin = TRUE
    ),
    shapes = list(
      list(
        type = "line",
        xref = "paper",
        x0 = 0,
        x1 = 1,
        yref = "y",
        y0 = 1,
        y1 = 1,
        line = list(color = "#555555", dash = "dash", width = 1)
      )
    ),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.2),
    margin = list(l = 90, r = 20, t = 60, b = 110),
    font = list(size = 12)
  ) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE)
```

Source: The New York Times. The dashed line marks 1 case per 100,000 per day (7-day average). Same-date ties are ranked by the crossing-day rate. Zero values are omitted on the log scale.

Using the threshold of 1 daily reported case per 100,000, the selected states were Washington, New York, Louisiana, New Jersey, and Michigan. Washington crossed first on March 15, 2020. Michigan and Vermont both crossed on March 21; the stated tie-breaking rule selected Michigan. These results depend on the chosen threshold and reported case data.
